# git-graph manual

**Content**

* [Overview](#overview)
* [Options](#options)
* [Formatting](#formatting)
* [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models)

## Overview

The most basic usage is to simply call git-graph from inside a Git repository:

```
git-graph
```

This works also deeper down the directory tree, so no need to be in the repository's root folder.

Alternatively, the path to the repository to visualize can be specified with option `--path`:

```
git-graph --path "path/to/repo"
```

**Branching models**

The above call assumes the GitFlow branching model (the default). Different branching models can be used with the option `--model` or `-m`:

```
git-graph --model simple
```

To *permanently* set the branching model for a repository, use subcommand `model`, like

```
git-graph model simple
```

Use the subcommand without argument to view the currently set branching model of a repository:

```
git-graph model
```

To view all available branching models, use option `--list` or `-l` of the subcommand:

```
git-graph model --list
```

For **defining your own models**, see section [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models).

**Styles**

Git-graph supports different styles. Besides the default `normal` (alias `thin`), supported styles are `round`, `bold`, `double` and `ascii`. Use a style with option `--style` or `-s`:

```
git-graph --style round
```

![styles](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44003176/103467621-357ce780-4d51-11eb-8ff9-dd7be8b40f84.png)

Style `ascii` can be used for devices and media that do not support Unicode/UTF-8 characters. 

**Formatting**

Git-graph supports predefined as well as custom commit formatting through option `--format`. Available presets follow Git: `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. For details and custom formatting, see section [Formatting](#formatting).

For a complete list of all available options, see the next section [Options](#options).

**Tags**

Internally, all tags start with `tag/`. To match Git tags, use RegEx patterns like `^tags/.*$`. However, only tags that are not on any branch are ordered and colored separately.

**Colors**

**Terminal colors** support the 8 system color names `black`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `magenta`, `cyan` and `white`, as well as each of them prefixed with `bright_` (e.g. `bright_blue`).

Further, indices of the 256-color palette are supported. For a full list, see [here](https://jonasjacek.github.io/colors/). Indices must be quoted as strings (e.g. `'16'`)

**SVG colors** support all named web colors (full list [here](https://htmlcolorcodes.com/color-names/)), as well as RGB colors in hex notation, like `#ffffff`.

# Overview

To generate a graph, [GitGraph::new()] will read the repository
and assign every commit to a single branch.

It takes the following steps to generate the graph

- Identify branches
- Sort branches by persistence
- Trace branches to commits
- Filtering and indexing

## Identify branches
Local and remote git-branches and tags are used as candidates for branches.
A branch can be identified by a merge commit, even though no current git-branch
refers to it.

## Sort branches by persistence
Each branch is assigned a persistence which can be configured by settings.
Think of persistence as z-order where lower values take preceedence.
**TODO** Merge branch

## Trace branches to commits
The branches now get to pick their commits, in order of persistence. Each
branch starts with a head, and follow the primary parent while it is
available. It stops when the parent is a commit already assigned to a branch.

# Branch sorting
The goal of this algorithm is to assign a column number to each tracked branch so that they can be visualized linearly without overlapping in the graph. It uses a shortest-first scheduling strategy (optionally longest-first and with forward/backward start sorting).

## Initialization
- occupied: A vector of vectors of vectors of tuples. 
The outer vector is indexed by the branch's order_group (determined by branch_order based on the settings.branches.order). 
Each inner vector represents a column within that order group, 
and the tuples (start, end) store the range of commits occupied by a branch in that column. 

## Preparing Branches for Sorting
- It creates branches_sort, a vector of tuples containing the branch index, its start commit index (range.0), its end commit index (range.1), its source order group, and its target order group. 
- It filters out branches that don't have a defined range (meaning they weren't associated with any commits). 
## Sorting Branches
- The branches_sort vector is sorted based on a key that prioritizes: 
    1. The maximum of the source and target order groups. This likely aims to keep related branches (e.g., those involved in merges) closer together. 
    2. The length of the branch's lifespan (end - start commit index), either shortest-first or longest-first based on the shortest_first setting. 
    3. The starting commit index, either forward or backward based on the forward setting.

## Formatting

Formatting can be specified with the `--format` option.

Predefined formats are `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. They should behave like the Git formatting presets described in the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

**oneline**

```
<hash> [<refs>] <title line>
```

**short**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>

<title line>
```

**medium**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

**full**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Commit: <committer>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

### Custom formatting

Formatting strings use a subset of the placeholders available in `git log --format="..."`:

| Placeholder | Replaced with                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| %n          | newline                                     |
| %H          | commit hash                                 |
| %h          | abbreviated commit hash                     |
| %P          | parent commit hashes                        |
| %p          | abbreviated parent commit hashes            |
| %d          | refs (branches, tags)                       |
| %s          | commit summary                              |
| %b          | commit message body                         |
| %B          | raw body (subject and body)                 |
| %an         | author name                                 |
| %ae         | author email                                |
| %ad         | author date                                 |
| %as         | author date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD`    |
| %ar         | author date, relative format (e.g., "21 hours ago") |
| %cn         | committer name                              |
| %ce         | committer email                             |
| %cd         | committer date                              |
| %cs         | committer date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| %cr         | committer date, relative format (e.g., "4 days ago") |

If you add a '+' (plus sign) after % of a placeholder, a line-feed is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

If you add a '-' (minus sign) after % of a placeholder, all consecutive line-feeds immediately preceding the expansion are deleted if and only if the placeholder expands to an empty string.

If you add a ' ' (space) after % of a placeholder, a space is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

See also the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

More formatting placeholders are planned for later releases.

**Examples**

Format recreating `oneline`:

```
git-graph --format "%h%d %s"
```

Format similar to `short`:

```
git-graph --format "commit %H%nAuthor: %an %ae%n%n    %s%n"
```

## Custom branching models

Branching models are configured using the files in `APP_DATA/git-graph/models`. 

* Windows: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\git-graph`
* Linux: `~/.config/git-graph`
* OSX: `~/Library/Application Support/git-graph`

File names of any `.toml` files in the `models` directory can be used in parameter `--model`, or via sub-command `model`. E.g., to use a branching model defined in `my-model.toml`, use:

```
git-graph --model my-model
```

**Branching model files** are in [TOML](https://toml.io/en/) format and have several sections, relying on Regular Expressions to categorize branches. The listing below shows the `git-flow` model (slightly abbreviated) with explanatory comments.

```toml
# RegEx patterns for branch groups by persistence, from most persistent
# to most short-leved branches. This is used to back-trace branches.
# Branches not matching any pattern are assumed least persistent.
persistence = [
    '^(master|main|trunk)$', # Matches exactly `master` or `main`  or `trunk`
    '^(develop|dev)$',
    '^feature.*$',     # Matches everything starting with `feature`
    '^release.*$',
    '^hotfix.*$',
    '^bugfix.*$',
]

# RegEx patterns for visual ordering of branches, from left to right.
# Here, `master`, `main` or `trunk` are shown left-most, followed by branches
# starting with `hotfix` or `release`, followed by `develop` or `dev`.
# Branches not matching any pattern (e.g. starting with `feature`)
# are displayed further to the right.
order = [
    '^(master|main|trunk)$',      # Matches exactly `master` or `main` or `trunk`
    '^(hotfix|release).*$', # Matches everything starting with `hotfix` or `release`
    '^(develop|dev)$',      # Matches exactly `develop` or `dev`
]

# Colors of branches in terminal output. 
# For supported colors, see section Colors (below this listing).
[terminal_colors]
# Each entry is composed of a RegEx pattern and a list of colors that
# will be used alternating (see e.g. `feature...`).
matches = [
    [
        '^(master|main|trunk)$',
        ['bright_blue'],
    ],
    [
        '^(develop|dev)$',
        ['bright_yellow'],
    ],
    [   # Branches obviously merged in from forks are prefixed with 'fork/'. 
        # The 'fork/' prefix is only available in order and colors, but not in persistence!
        '^(feature|fork/).*$',
        ['bright_magenta', 'bright_cyan'], # Multiple colors for alternating use
    ],
        [
        '^release.*$',
        ['bright_green'],
    ],
        [
        '^(bugfix|hotfix).*$',
        ['bright_red'],
    ],
    [
        '^tags/.*$',
        ['bright_green'],
    ],
]
# A list of colors that are used (alternating) for all branches
# not matching any of the above pattern. 
unknown = ['white']

# Colors of branches in SVG output. 
# Same structure as terminal_colors. 
# For supported colors, see section Colors (below this listing).
[svg_colors]
matches = [
    [
        '^(master|main|trunk)$',
        ['blue'],
    ],
    [ 
        '...',
    ]
]
unknown = ['gray']
```

**Tags**

Internally, all tags start with `tag/`. To match Git tags, use RegEx patterns like `^tags/.*$`. However, only tags that are not on any branch are ordered and colored separately.

**Colors**

**Terminal colors** support the 8 system color names `black`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `magenta`, `cyan` and `white`, as well as each of them prefixed with `bright_` (e.g. `bright_blue`).

Further, indices of the 256-color palette are supported. For a full list, see [here](https://jonasjacek.github.io/colors/). Indices must be quoted as strings (e.g. `'16'`)

**SVG colors** support all named web colors (full list [here](https://htmlcolorcodes.com/color-names/)), as well as RGB colors in hex notation, like `#ffffff`.

<output>

# Overview

To generate a graph, [GitGraph::new()] will read the repository
and assign every commit to a single branch.

It takes the following steps to generate the graph

- Identify branches
- Sort branches by persistence
- Trace branches to commits
- Filtering and indexing

## Identify branches
Local and remote git-branches and tags are used as candidates for branches.
A branch can be identified by a merge commit, even though no current git-branch
refers to it.

## Sort branches by persistence
Each branch is assigned a persistence which can be configured by settings.
Think of persistence as z-order where lower values take preceedence.
**TODO** Merge branch

## Trace branches to commits
The branches now get to pick their commits, in order of persistence. Each
branch starts with a head, and follow the primary parent while it is
available. It stops when the parent is a commit already assigned to a branch.
**TODO** Duplicate branch names
**TODO** Handle visual artifacts on merge

## Filtering and indexing
Commits that have not been assigned a branch is filtered out.
An *index_map* is created to map from original commit index, to filtered
commit index.
**TODO** what? why? Would it not be better to track from child/heads instead of every single commit in repo?




# Branch sorting
The goal of this algorithm is to assign a column number to each tracked branch so that they can be visualized linearly without overlapping in the graph. It uses a shortest-first scheduling strategy (optionally longest-first and with forward/backward start sorting).

## Initialization
- occupied: A vector of vectors of vectors of tuples. 
The outer vector is indexed by the branch's order_group (determined by branch_order based on the settings.branches.order). 
Each inner vector represents a column within that order group, 
and the tuples (start, end) store the range of commits occupied by a branch in that column. 

## Preparing Branches for Sorting
- It creates branches_sort, a vector of tuples containing the branch index, its start commit index (range.0), its end commit index (range.1), its source order group, and its target order group. 
- It filters out branches that don't have a defined range (meaning they weren't associated with any commits). 
## Sorting Branches
- The branches_sort vector is sorted based on a key that prioritizes: 
    1. The maximum of the source and target order groups. This likely aims to keep related branches (e.g., those involved in merges) closer together. 
    2. The length of the branch's lifespan (end - start commit index), either shortest-first or longest-first based on the shortest_first setting. 
    3. The starting commit index, either forward or backward based on the forward setting. 
</output>

# git-graph manual$
$
**Content**$
$
* [Overview](#overview)$
* [Options](#options)$
* [Formatting](#formatting)$
* [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models)$
$
## Overview$
$
The most basic usage is to simply call git-graph from inside a Git repository:$
$
```$
git-graph$
```$
$
This works also deeper down the directory tree, so no need to be in the repository's root folder.$
$
Alternatively, the path to the repository to visualize can be specified with option `--path`:$
$
```$
git-graph --path "path/to/repo"$
```$
$
**Branching models**$
$
The above call assumes the GitFlow branching model (the default). Different branching models can be used with the option `--model` or `-m`:$
$
```$
git-graph --model simple$
```$
$
To *permanently* set the branching model for a repository, use subcommand `model`, like$
$
```$
git-graph model simple$
```$
$
Use the subcommand without argument to view the currently set branching model of a repository:$
$
```$
git-graph model$
```$
$
To view all available branching models, use option `--list` or `-l` of the subcommand:$
$
```$
git-graph model --list$
```$
$
For **defining your own models**, see section [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models).$
$
**Styles**$
$
Git-graph supports different styles. Besides the default `normal` (alias `thin`), supported styles are `round`, `bold`, `double` and `ascii`. Use a style with option `--style` or `-s`:$
$
```$
git-graph --style round$
```$
$
![styles](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44003176/103467621-357ce780-4d51-11eb-8ff9-dd7be8b40f84.png)$
$
Style `ascii` can be used for devices and media that do not support Unicode/UTF-8 characters. $
$
**Formatting**$
$
Git-graph supports predefined as well as custom commit formatting through option `--format`. Available presets follow Git: `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. For details and custom formatting, see section [Formatting](#formatting).$
$
For a complete list of all available options, see the next section [Options](#options).$
$
## Options$
$
All options are explained in the CLI help. View it with `git-graph -h`:$
$

For longer explanations, use `git-graph --help`.

## Formatting

Formatting can be specified with the `--format` option.

Predefined formats are `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. They should behave like the Git formatting presets described in the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

**oneline**

```
<hash> [<refs>] <title line>
```

**short**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>

<title line>
```

**medium**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

**full**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Commit: <committer>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

### Custom formatting

Formatting strings use a subset of the placeholders available in `git log --format="..."`:

| Placeholder | Replaced with                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| %n          | newline                                     |
| %H          | commit hash                                 |
| %h          | abbreviated commit hash                     |
| %P          | parent commit hashes                        |
| %p          | abbreviated parent commit hashes            |
| %d          | refs (branches, tags)                       |
| %s          | commit summary                              |
| %b          | commit message body                         |
| %B          | raw body (subject and body)                 |
| %an         | author name                                 |
| %ae         | author email                                |
| %ad         | author date                                 |
| %as         | author date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD`    |
| %ar         | author date, relative format (e.g., "21 hours ago") |
| %cn         | committer name                              |
| %ce         | committer email                             |
| %cd         | committer date                              |
| %cs         | committer date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| %cr         | committer date, relative format (e.g., "4 days ago") |

If you add a '+' (plus sign) after % of a placeholder, a line-feed is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

If you add a '-' (minus sign) after % of a placeholder, all consecutive line-feeds immediately preceding the expansion are deleted if and only if the placeholder expands to an empty string.

If you add a ' ' (space) after % of a placeholder, a space is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

See also the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

More formatting placeholders are planned for later releases.

**Examples**

Format recreating `oneline`:

```
git-graph --format "%h%d %s"
```

Format similar to `short`:

```
git-graph --format "commit %H%nAuthor: %an %ae%n%n    %s%n"
```

## Custom branching models

Branching models are configured using the files in `APP_DATA/git-graph/models`. 

* Windows: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\git-graph`
* Linux: `~/.config/git-graph`
* OSX: `~/Library/Application Support/git-graph`

File names of any `.toml` files in the `models` directory can be used in parameter `--model`, or via sub-command `model`. E.g., to use a branching model defined in `my-model.toml`, use:

```
git-graph --model my-model
```

**Branching model files** are in [TOML](https://toml.io/en/) format and have several sections, relying on Regular Expressions to categorize branches. The listing below shows the `git-flow` model (slightly abbreviated) with explanatory comments.

```toml
# RegEx patterns for branch groups by persistence, from most persistent
# to most short-leved branches. This is used to back-trace branches.
# Branches not matching any pattern are assumed least persistent.
persistence = [
    '^(master|main|trunk)$', # Matches exactly `master` or `main`  or `trunk`
    '^(develop|dev)$',
    '^feature.*$',     # Matches everything starting with `feature`
    '^release.*$',
    '^hotfix.*$',
    '^bugfix.*$',
]

# RegEx patterns for visual ordering of branches, from left to right.
# Here, `master`, `main` or `trunk` are shown left-most, followed by branches
# starting with `hotfix` or `release`, followed by `develop` or `dev`.
# Branches not matching any pattern (e.g. starting with `feature`)
# are displayed further to the right.
order = [
    '^(master|main|trunk)$',      # Matches exactly `master` or `main` or `trunk`
    '^(hotfix|release).*$', # Matches everything starting with `hotfix` or `release`
    '^(develop|dev)$',      # Matches exactly `develop` or `dev`
]

# Colors of branches in terminal output. 
# For supported colors, see section Colors (below this listing).
[terminal_colors]
# Each entry is composed of a RegEx pattern and a list of colors that
# will be used alternating (see e.g. `feature...`).
matches = [
    [
        '^(master|main|trunk)$',
        ['bright_blue'],
    ],
    [
        '^(develop|dev)$',
        ['bright_yellow'],
    ],
    [   # Branches obviously merged in from forks are prefixed with 'fork/'. 
        # The 'fork/' prefix is only available in order and colors, but not in persistence!
        '^(feature|fork/).*$',
        ['bright_magenta', 'bright_cyan'], # Multiple colors for alternating use
    ],
        [
        '^release.*$',
        ['bright_green'],
    ],
        [
        '^(bugfix|hotfix).*$',
        ['bright_red'],
    ],
    [
        '^tags/.*$',
        ['bright_green'],
    ],
]
# A list of colors that are used (alternating) for all branches
# not matching any of the above pattern. 
unknown = ['white']
</output>

    # Validate format abbreviation: first char maps to preset if single char or full name

def get_commit_data(repo_path, commit_hash):
    # Use git show -s with pretty format to get commit details
    # We'll call git log -1 with custom format to get fields
    # Fields we need: H, h, P, p, an, ae, ad, as, ar, cn, ce, cd, cs, cr, s, b, B, d
    # We can use git show with --pretty=format: plus terminators
    # Use %x00 as separator to avoid newline issues in body

    # Use git log -1 with format that includes all needed placeholders separated by \0
    # Note: %s is subject (first line), %b is body (without subject), %B is raw body (subject+body)
    # %an, %ae, %ad, %as, %ar etc.

    fmt = "%H%x00%h%x00%P%x00%p%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%ad%x00%as%x00%ar%x00%cn%x00%ce%x00%cd%x00%cs%x00%cr%x00%s%x00%b%x00%B%x00%d"
    # Need to ensure %d is not expanded with extra? We'll get it but we will recompute ourselves.
    # Use git show
    result = sp.run(["git","show","-s","--pretty=format:"+fmt, commit_hash], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None
    out = result.stdout
    # Split by \0 ; should have 18 parts? Let's count: H,h,P,p,an,ae,ad,as,ar,cn,ce,cd,cs,cr,s,b,B,d => 18 fields? Actually fmt has 17 placeholders? Count: H(1),h(2),P(3),p(4),an(5),ae(6),ad(7),as(8),ar(9),cn(10),ce(11),cd(12),cs(13),cr(14),s(15),b(16),B(17),d(18) => 18
    parts = out.split("\x00")
    # Pad if missing
    while len(parts) < 18:
        parts.append("")
    data = {
        "H": parts[0],
        "h": parts[1],
        "P": parts[2],
        "p": parts[3],
        "an": parts[4],
        "ae": parts[5],
        "ad": parts[6],
        "as": parts[7],
        "ar": parts[8],
        "cn": parts[9],
        "ce": parts[10],
        "cd": parts[11],
        "cs": parts[12],
        "cr": parts[13],
        "s": parts[14],
        "b": parts[15],
        "B": parts[16],
        "d": parts[17], # raw git's d, but we will not use directly
    }
    # Also need parents list
    data["parents"] = data["P"].split() if data["P"] else []
    data["parents_abbrev"] = data["p"].split() if data["p"] else []
    return data


# Model handling

def load_model_config(model_name):
    d = get_models_dir()
    path = d / f"{model_name}.toml"
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    # Try to parse minimal TOML: we only need persistence, order, terminal_colors, svg_colors
    # Use simple parser without external deps
    try:
        content = path.read_text()
        # Use tomllib if available (python 3.11+), else fallback to tomli
        try:
            import tomllib
            data = tomllib.loads(content)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            data = tomli.loads(content)
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        # If parsing fails, return empty
        return {}

def get_model_persistence_order(model_name):
    cfg = load_model_config(model_name)
    if cfg is None:
        return [], []
    persistence = cfg.get("persistence", [])
    order = cfg.get("order", [])
    # Ensure list
    if not isinstance(persistence, list):
        persistence = []
    if not isinstance(order, list):
        order = []
    return persistence, order

def get_model_colors(model_name, is_svg=False):
    cfg = load_model_config(model_name)
    if cfg is None:
        return [], []
    key = "svg_colors" if is_svg else "terminal_colors"
    colors_cfg = cfg.get(key, {})
    matches = colors_cfg.get("matches", [])
    unknown = colors_cfg.get("unknown", ["white" if not is_svg else "gray"])
    return matches, unknown

def get_models_dir():
    # Use HOME
    home = pathlib.Path.home()
    cfg = home / ".config" / "git-graph" / "models"
    if cfg.exists():
        return cfg
    # also try XDG?
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        p = pathlib.Path(xdg) / "git-graph" / "models"
        if p.exists():
            return p
    return cfg

def list_models():
    d = get_models_dir()
    if not d.exists():
        return []
    # Use os.listdir unsorted to match original behaviour (directory entry order)
    try:
        files = os.listdir(d)
    except:
        files = []
    models = []
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith(".toml"):
            models.append(f[:-5])
    return models

def get_available_models_str():
    models = list_models()
    return ", ".join(models)

    # Early handling for `help` subcommand as first arg without dash: we already handle in parse but need to differentiate

    if argv and argv[0] == "help":

    # We'll do manual parse with extra state for wrap
    opts = parse_args_manual(argv)

    if opts.get("subcommand") == "model":

    # Validate model option if supplied

    # Validate style
    style = opts.get("style","normal")

    # We'll map first char to full name if unique
    style_map = {
        "n": "normal", "t": "thin", "r": "round", "b": "bold", "d": "double", "a": "ascii",
        "normal": "normal", "thin": "normal", # thin alias normal? Actually normal and thin same? Both represent normal.
        "round": "round", "bold": "bold", "double": "double", "ascii": "ascii"
    }
    # Original says normal/thin same, so both map to normal
    # For style input, if it's single char, map via first char, else exact
    style_input = style.lower()
    if len(style_input) == 1:

        if style_input in style_map:
            style = style_map[style_input]
        else:
            eprint(f"Unknown characters/style '{style}'. Must be one of [normal|thin|round|bold|double|ascii]")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        if style_input not in ["normal","thin","round","bold","double","ascii"]:
            eprint(f"Unknown characters/style '{style}'. Must be one of [normal|thin|round|bold|double|ascii]")
            sys.exit(1)
        # Map thin to normal
        if style_input == "thin":
            style = "normal"
        else:
            style = style_input

    # Validate color (unless no_color overrides)
    color = opts.get("color","auto")

    if not no_color:

    # Validate max-count
    max_count = opts.get("max_count")
    if max_count is not None:
        try:
            iv = int(max_count)
            if iv <= 0:
                raise ValueError
            opts["max_count_int"] = iv
        except:
            # Check if max_count was string like "foo" -> this error
            # But if it was "-1" we already handled as unexpected argument earlier, so here only for non-negative?
            eprint(f"Option max-count must be a positive number, but got '{max_count}'")
            sys.exit(1)

    # Validate wrap
    wrap_args = opts.get("wrap_args")
    wrap_present = opts.get("wrap_present", False)
    # Actually opts wrap_args is collected only if --wrap flag present. We need to know if flag was present even with empty args.
    # In parse, we set wrap_args even if empty list when flag present. So we can check if "wrap_args" in opts and flag present.
    # We'll have a separate flag wrap_flag
    if opts.get("wrap_flag"):
        wrap_str = " ".join(wrap_args) if wrap_args else ""
        # If no args, treat as default auto 0 8 (no error)
        if not wrap_args:
            wrap_parsed = ("auto", None, 0, 8)
            opts["wrap_parsed"] = wrap_parsed
        else:
            # Need to parse wrap_args list
            # tokens = wrap_args
            # Validate
            # Use parse_wrap function that takes list
            parsed, err = parse_wrap(wrap_args)
            if err:
                eprint(err)
                sys.exit(1)
            opts["wrap_parsed"] = parsed
    else:
        # Default wrap auto 0 8
        opts["wrap_parsed"] = ("auto", None, 0, 8)

    # Validate format abbreviation: first char maps to preset if single char or full name
    fmt = opts.get("format","oneline")
    # Original supports first character abbreviation, e.g., '-f m' => medium. But also full string like "oneline", "short", etc.
    # If fmt is single char 'o','s','m','f' -> map to preset
    # If fmt is longer but starts with those letters? We saw that "oneline" works, "o" works, but "ooo" treated as literal, not preset. So only exact match for preset names or single char.
    # So we handle:
    fmt_lower = fmt.lower()
    if fmt_lower in ("o","oneline"):
        fmt = "oneline"
    elif fmt_lower in ("s","short"):
        fmt = "short"
    elif fmt_lower in ("m","medium"):
        fmt = "medium"
    elif fmt_lower in ("f","full"):
        fmt = "full"
    else:
        # Keep as custom format string (even if starts with o/s/m/f but not exact)
        fmt = fmt
    opts["format_parsed"] = fmt

    # Now we need to find repo and generate graph
    repo_path, err = find_repo_path(opts.get("path","."))
    if err:

    try:
        generate_and_print(repo_path, opts)
    except Exception as e:

        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)

def parse_args_manual(argv):
    opts = {
        "path": ".",
        "skip_validation": False,
        "model": None,
        "max_count": None,
        "color": "auto",
        "no_color": False,
        "wrap_args": [],
        "wrap_flag": False,
        "format": "oneline",
        "reverse": False,
        "local": False,
        "svg": False,
        "debug": False,
        "sparse": False,
        "style": "normal",
        "subcommand": None,
        "sub_args": [],
    }

    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        # Detect subcommand start if not already
        if opts["subcommand"] is None and arg in ("model","help"):
            opts["subcommand"] = arg
            opts["sub_args"] = argv[i+1:]
            break

        # Handle long options with =
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            if "=" in arg:
                name, val = arg.split("=",1)
                # Insert val as next token
                argv = argv[:i] + [name, val] + argv[i+1:]
                n = len(argv)
                arg = name
                # continue to handle name
            if arg == "--path":
                if i+1 >= n or argv[i+1].startswith("-"):
                    eprint(f"error: a value is required for '--path <path>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
                opts["path"] = argv[i+1]
                i += 2
                continue
            elif arg == "--skip-repo-owner-validation":
                opts["skip_validation"] = True
                i += 1
                continue
            elif arg == "--model":
                if i+1 >= n or argv[i+1].startswith("-"):
                    eprint(f"error: a value is required for '--model <model>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
                opts["model"] = argv[i+1]
                i += 2
                continue
            elif arg == "--max-count":
                if i+1 >= n:
                    eprint(f"error: a value is required for '--max-count <n>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
                nxt = argv[i+1]

                continue
            elif arg == "--color":

                i += 2
                continue
            elif arg == "--no-color":
                opts["no_color"] = True
                i += 1
                continue
            elif arg == "--wrap":
                opts["wrap_flag"] = True
                collected = []
                j = i+1
                while j < n and len(collected) < 3:
                    nxt = argv[j]
                    if nxt.startswith("-"):
                        break
                    collected.append(nxt)
                    j += 1
                opts["wrap_args"] = collected
                i = j
                continue
            elif arg == "--format":

                    # But format string could be like "%h"%? It starts with %, not -. So handle.

                opts["format"] = argv[i+1]

                continue

                continue

                sys.exit(2)
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            # Short options
            # Handle -h and -V early? But they print help/version

            chars = arg[1:]

                    else:

                            sys.exit(2)
                        opts["model"] = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                        idx += 1
                        break
                elif c == "n":

                    opts["wrap_args"] = collected
                    i = j - 1
                    idx += 1
                    break
                elif c == "f":

                        break
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= n or argv[i+1].startswith("-"):
                            eprint(f"error: a value is required for '--format <format>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
                            sys.exit(2)
                        opts["format"] = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                        idx += 1
                        break
                elif c == "r":
                    opts["reverse"] = True
                    idx += 1
                elif c == "l":
                    opts["local"] = True
                    idx += 1
                elif c == "d":
                    opts["debug"] = True
                    idx += 1
                elif c == "S":
                    opts["sparse"] = True

                elif c == "s":
                    if idx+1 < len(chars):

                    else:

                        opts["style"] = argv[i+1]

def get_branches_and_tags(repo_path, local_only=False):

    # Use git for-each-ref

    # Remote branches: refs/remotes/*
    # Tags: refs/tags/*
    branches = [] # list of (name, hash, is_remote, is_tag)

    result = sp.run(["git","for-each-ref","--format=%(refname) %(objectname)","refs/heads"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True)

            ref, hsh = line.split()
            name = ref.replace("refs/heads/","")

        result = sp.run(["git","for-each-ref","--format=%(refname) %(objectname)","refs/remotes"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True)

def get_commit_data(repo_path, commit_hash):
    # Use git show -s with pretty format to get commit details
    # We'll call git log -1 with custom format to get fields
    # Fields we need: H, h, P, p, an, ae, ad, as, ar, cn, ce, cd, cs, cr, s, b, B, d
    # We can use git show with --pretty=format: plus terminators
    # Use %x00 as separator to avoid newline issues in body

    # Use git log -1 with format that includes all needed placeholders separated by \0
    # Note: %s is subject (first line), %b is body (without subject), %B is raw body (subject+body)
    # %an, %ae, %ad, %as, %ar etc.

    fmt = "%H%x00%h%x00%P%x00%p%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%ad%x00%as%x00%ar%x00%cn%x00%ce%x00%cd%x00%cs%x00%cr%x00%s%x00%b%x00%B%x00%d"
    # Need to ensure %d is not expanded with extra? We'll get it but we will recompute ourselves.
    # Use git show
    result = sp.run(["git","show","-s","--pretty=format:"+fmt, commit_hash], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None
    out = result.stdout
    # Split by \0 ; should have 18 parts? Let's count: H,h,P,p,an,ae,ad,as,ar,cn,ce,cd,cs,cr,s,b,B,d => 18 fields? Actually fmt has 17 placeholders? Count: H(1),h(2),P(3),p(4),an(5),ae(6),ad(7),as(8),ar(9),cn(10),ce(11),cd(12),cs(13),cr(14),s(15),b(16),B(17),d(18) => 18
    parts = out.split("\x00")
    # Pad if missing
    while len(parts) < 18:
        parts.append("")
    data = {
        "H": parts[0],
        "h": parts[1],
        "P": parts[2],
        "p": parts[3],
        "an": parts[4],
        "ae": parts[5],
        "ad": parts[6],
        "as": parts[7],
        "ar": parts[8],
        "cn": parts[9],
        "ce": parts[10],
        "cd": parts[11],
        "cs": parts[12],
        "cr": parts[13],
        "s": parts[14],
        "b": parts[15],
        "B": parts[16],
        "d": parts[17], # raw git's d, but we will not use directly
    }
    # Also need parents list
    data["parents"] = data["P"].split() if data["P"] else []
    data["parents_abbrev"] = data["p"].split() if data["p"] else []
    return data


# Model handling

def load_model_config(model_name):
    d = get_models_dir()
    path = d / f"{model_name}.toml"
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    # Try to parse minimal TOML: we only need persistence, order, terminal_colors, svg_colors
    # Use simple parser without external deps
    try:
        content = path.read_text()
        # Use tomllib if available (python 3.11+), else fallback to tomli
        try:
            import tomllib
            data = tomllib.loads(content)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            data = tomli.loads(content)
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        # If parsing fails, return empty
        return {}

def get_model_persistence_order(model_name):
    cfg = load_model_config(model_name)
    if cfg is None:
        return [], []
    persistence = cfg.get("persistence", [])
    order = cfg.get("order", [])
    # Ensure list
    if not isinstance(persistence, list):
        persistence = []
    if not isinstance(order, list):
        order = []
    return persistence, order

def get_model_colors(model_name, is_svg=False):
    cfg = load_model_config(model_name)
    if cfg is None:
        return [], []
    key = "svg_colors" if is_svg else "terminal_colors"
    colors_cfg = cfg.get(key, {})
    matches = colors_cfg.get("matches", [])
    unknown = colors_cfg.get("unknown", ["white" if not is_svg else "gray"])
    return matches, unknown

# Overview

To generate a graph, [GitGraph::new()] will read the repository
and assign every commit to a single branch.

It takes the following steps to generate the graph

- Identify branches
- Sort branches by persistence
- Trace branches to commits
- Filtering and indexing

## Identify branches
Local and remote git-branches and tags are used as candidates for branches.
A branch can be identified by a merge commit, even though no current git-branch
refers to it.

## Sort branches by persistence
Each branch is assigned a persistence which can be configured by settings.
Think of persistence as z-order where lower values take preceedence.
**TODO** Merge branch

## Trace branches to commits
The branches now get to pick their commits, in order of persistence. Each
branch starts with a head, and follow the primary parent while it is
available. It stops when the parent is a commit already assigned to a branch.
**TODO** Duplicate branch names
**TODO** Handle visual artifacts on merge

## Filtering and indexing
Commits that have not been assigned a branch is filtered out.
An *index_map* is created to map from original commit index, to filtered
commit index.
**TODO** what? why? Would it not be better to track from child/heads instead of every single commit in repo?




# Branch sorting
The goal of this algorithm is to assign a column number to each tracked branch so that they can be visualized linearly without overlapping in the graph. It uses a shortest-first scheduling strategy (optionally longest-first and with forward/backward start sorting).

## Initialization
- occupied: A vector of vectors of vectors of tuples. 
The outer vector is indexed by the branch's order_group (determined by branch_order based on the settings.branches.order). 
Each inner vector represents a column within that order group, 
and the tuples (start, end) store the range of commits occupied by a branch in that column. 

## Preparing Branches for Sorting
- It creates branches_sort, a vector of tuples containing the branch index, its start commit index (range.0), its end commit index (range.1), its source order group, and its target order group. 
- It filters out branches that don't have a defined range (meaning they weren't associated with any commits). 
## Sorting Branches
- The branches_sort vector is sorted based on a key that prioritizes: 
    1. The maximum of the source and target order groups. This likely aims to keep related branches (e.g., those involved in merges) closer together. 
    2. The length of the branch's lifespan (end - start commit index), either shortest-first or longest-first based on the shortest_first setting. 
    3. The starting commit index, either forward or backward based on the forward setting.

def eprint(*args, **kwargs):
    print(*args, file=sys.stderr, **kwargs)

def get_models_dir():
    home = pathlib.Path.home()
    cfg = home / ".config" / "git-graph" / "models"
    if cfg.exists():
        return cfg
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        p = pathlib.Path(xdg) / "git-graph" / "models"
        if p.exists():
            return p
    return cfg

def list_models():
    d = get_models_dir()
    if not d.exists():
        return []
    try:
        files = os.listdir(d)
    except:
        files = []
    models = []
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith(".toml"):
            models.append(f[:-5])
    return models

def find_repo_path(start_path):
    p = pathlib.Path(start_path)
    if not p.exists():
        return None, f"ERROR: failed to resolve path '{start_path}': No such file or directory\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path"
    result = subprocess.run(["git","rev-parse","--show-toplevel"], cwd=str(p), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None, f"ERROR: could not find repository at '{start_path}'\n       Navigate into a repository before running git-graph, or use option --path"
    toplevel = result.stdout.strip()
    return toplevel, None

def parse_wrap(args):
    if not args:
        return ("auto", None, 0, 8), None
    raw = " ".join(args)
    tokens = args
    if len(tokens) > 3:
        return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
    first = tokens[0].lower()
    if first in ("auto","none"):
        mode = first
        if len(tokens) == 1:
            return (mode, None, 0, 8), None
        elif len(tokens) == 2:
            try:
                indent1 = int(tokens[1])
            except:
                return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
            return (mode, None, indent1, 8), None
        else:
            try:
                indent1 = int(tokens[1]); indent2 = int(tokens[2])
            except:
                return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
            return (mode, None, indent1, indent2), None
    else:
        try:
            width = int(first)
        except:
            return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
        if len(tokens) == 1:
            return ("fixed", width, 0, 8), None
        elif len(tokens) == 2:
            try:
                indent1 = int(tokens[1])
            except:
                return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
            return ("fixed", width, indent1, 8), None
        else:
            try:
                indent1 = int(tokens[1]); indent2 = int(tokens[2])
            except:
                return None, f"ERROR: Can't parse option --wrap '{raw}' to integers."
            return ("fixed", width, indent1, indent2), None

def handle_model_subcommand(sub_args, global_opts):
    for a in sub_args:
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            print(MODEL_HELP, end="")
            sys.exit(0)
    list_flag=False
    positional=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(sub_args):
        a=sub_args[i]
        if a in ("-l","--list"):
            list_flag=True; i+=1
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{a}' as a value, use '-- {a}'\n\nUsage: executable model [OPTIONS] [model]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
            sys.exit(2)
        else:
            positional.append(a); i+=1
    if list_flag:
        if len(positional) > 1:
            eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{positional[1]}' found\n\nUsage: executable model --list [model]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
            sys.exit(2)
        models=list_models()
        for m in models:
            print(m)
        sys.exit(0)
    if len(positional)==0:
        repo_path, err = find_repo_path(global_opts.get("path","."))
        if err:
            eprint(err); sys.exit(1)
        cfg = pathlib.Path(repo_path) / ".git" / "git-graph.toml"
        if cfg.exists():
            try:
                content=cfg.read_text()
                m=re.search(r'model\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', content)
                if m:
                    sys.stdout.write(m.group(1)); sys.exit(0)
                else:
                    sys.stdout.write("No branching model set"); sys.exit(0)
            except:
                sys.stdout.write("No branching model set"); sys.exit(0)
        else:
            sys.stdout.write("No branching model set"); sys.exit(0)
    elif len(positional)==1:
        model_name=positional[0]
        available=list_models()
        if model_name not in available:
            eprint(f"ERROR: No branching model named '{model_name}' found in {get_models_dir()}\n       Available models are: {', '.join(available)}")
            sys.exit(1)
        repo_path, err = find_repo_path(global_opts.get("path","."))
        if err:
            eprint(err); sys.exit(1)
        cfg = pathlib.Path(repo_path) / ".git" / "git-graph.toml"
        cfg.write_text(f'model = "{model_name}"\n')
        eprint(f"Branching model set to '{model_name}'")
        sys.exit(0)
    else:
        eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{positional[1]}' found\n\nUsage: executable model [OPTIONS] [model]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.")
        sys.exit(2)

def load_model_config(mn):
    d=get_models_dir()
    p=d/f"{mn}.toml"
    if not p.exists():
        return None
    try:
        t=p.read_text()
        try:
            import tomllib
            data=tomllib.loads(t)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            data=tomli.loads(t)
        return data
    except:
        return {}
def get_model_persistence_order(mn):
    cfg=load_model_config(mn)
    if cfg is None:
        return [],[]
    pers=cfg.get("persistence",[])
    order=cfg.get("order",[])
    if not isinstance(pers,list): pers=[]
    if not isinstance(order,list): order=[]
    return pers,order
def get_branches_and_tags(rp,local_only=False):
    branches=[]
    r=subprocess.run(["git","for-each-ref","--format=%(refname) %(objectname)","refs/heads"],cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.stdout:
        for line in r.stdout.strip().splitlines():
            if not line: continue
            ref,hsh=line.split()
            name=ref.replace("refs/heads/","")
            branches.append((name,hsh,False,False))
    if not local_only:
        r=subprocess.run(["git","for-each-ref","--format=%(refname) %(objectname)","refs/remotes"],cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
        if r.stdout:
            for line in r.stdout.strip().splitlines():
                if not line: continue
                ref,hsh=line.split()
                name=ref.replace("refs/remotes/","")
                branches.append((name,hsh,True,False))
    r=subprocess.run(["git","for-each-ref","--format=%(refname) %(objectname) %(*objectname)","refs/tags"],cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    tags=[]
    if r.stdout:
        for line in r.stdout.strip().splitlines():
            if not line: continue
            parts=line.split()
            ref=parts[0];obj=parts[1];peeled=parts[2] if len(parts)>2 else ""
            name=ref.replace("refs/tags/","")
            hsh=peeled if peeled else obj
            tags.append((name,hsh))
            branches.append((f"tags/{name}",hsh,False,True))
    head_branch=None;head_hash=None
    r=subprocess.run(["git","rev-parse","--abbrev-ref","HEAD"],cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.stdout:
        a=r.stdout.strip()
        head_branch=a if a!="HEAD" else "HEAD"
    r=subprocess.run(["git","rev-parse","HEAD"],cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.stdout:
        head_hash=r.stdout.strip()
    from collections import defaultdict
    commit_to_refs=defaultdict(list)
    for name,hsh,isr,ist in branches:
        commit_to_refs[hsh].append((name,isr,ist))

def assign_branches(rp,commits,branches,tags,commit_to_refs,head_branch,head_hash,mn,local_only):
    pers,order=get_model_persistence_order(mn)
    import re
    prx=[]
    for pat in pers:
        try: prx.append(re.compile(pat))
        except: prx.append(re.compile(re.escape(pat)))
    orx=[]
    for pat in order:
        try: orx.append(re.compile(pat))
        except: orx.append(re.compile(re.escape(pat)))
    def prank(name):
        for i,rgx in enumerate(prx):
            if rgx.search(name):
                return i
        return len(prx)
    def orank(name):
        for i,rgx in enumerate(orx):
            if rgx.search(name):
                return i
        return len(orx)
    b_objs=[]
    for name,hsh,ir,it in branches:
        b_objs.append({"name":name,"hash":hsh,"is_remote":ir,"is_tag":it,"persistence_rank":prank(name),"order_rank":orank(name),"commits":[],"range":(None,None)})

    if local_only:
        cmd=["git","rev-list","--branches","--tags","--topo-order","--parents"]
    r=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=rp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode==0:
        for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
            parts=line.strip().split()
            if not parts: continue
            h=parts[0]; parents=parts[1:]
            parent_map[h]=parents

    for idx,br in enumerate(b_objs):
        h=br["hash"]
        if h not in cidx: continue
        cur=h
        while cur and cur not in assigned:
            assigned[cur]=idx
            br["commits"].append(cur)
            pars=parent_map.get(cur,[])
            if not pars: break

def sort_branches_for_display(b_objs):
    from collections import defaultdict
    filt=[b for b in b_objs if b["range"][0] is not None]
    groups=defaultdict(list)
    for b in filt:
        groups[b["order_rank"]].append(b)
    for grp,lst in groups.items():
        lst.sort(key=lambda x: ((x["range"][1]-x["range"][0]) if x["range"][0] is not None else 0, x["range"][0] if x["range"][0] is not None else 0))
    ogids=sorted(groups.keys())
    col={}
    gc=0
    for gid in ogids:
        lst=groups[gid]
        occ=[]
        for b in lst:
            s,e=b["range"]
            placed=False
            for ci,ivs in enumerate(occ):
                ov=False
                for (a,b2) in ivs:
                    if not (e < a or s > b2):
                        ov=True;break
                if not ov:
                    ivs.append((s,e))
                    col[b["name"]]=gc+ci
                    placed=True;break
            if not placed:
                occ.append([(s,e)])
                col[b["name"]]=gc+len(occ)-1
        gc+=len(occ)
    for b in b_objs:
        if b["name"] not in col:
            col[b["name"]]=99
    return col

def expand_format_string(fmt,cd,refs_str):
    pmap={"H":cd.get("H",""),"h":cd.get("h",""),"P":cd.get("P",""),"p":cd.get("p",""),"d":refs_str,"s":cd.get("s",""),"b":cd.get("b",""),"B":cd.get("B",""),"an":cd.get("an",""),"ae":cd.get("ae",""),"ad":cd.get("ad",""),"as":cd.get("as",""),"ar":cd.get("ar",""),"cn":cd.get("cn",""),"ce":cd.get("ce",""),"cd":cd.get("cd",""),"cs":cd.get("cs",""),"cr":cd.get("cr",""),"n":"\n","%":"%"}
    res="";i=0;n=len(fmt)
    while i<n:
        if fmt[i]!="%":
            res+=fmt[i];i+=1;continue
        if i+1>=n:
            res+="%";i+=1;continue
        if fmt[i+1]=="%":
            res+="%";i+=2;continue
        mod=None;j=i+1
        if j<n and fmt[j] in ("+","-"," "):
            mod=fmt[j];j+=1
            if j>=n:
                res+="%"+mod;i=j;continue
        matched=None
        if j+1<n:
            two=fmt[j:j+2]
            if two in ("an","ae","ad","as","ar","cn","ce","cd","cs","cr"):
                matched=two;j+=2
            else:
                c=fmt[j]
                if c in ("H","h","P","p","d","s","b","B","n"):
                    matched=c;j+=1
                else:
                    res+=fmt[i:j+1];i=j+1;continue
        else:
            c=fmt[j]
            if c in ("H","h","P","p","d","s","b","B","n"):
                matched=c;j+=1
            else:
                res+=fmt[i:j+1];i=j+1;continue
        if matched is None:
            res+=fmt[i:j];i=j;continue
        exp=pmap.get(matched,"")
        if mod=="+":
            if exp!="":
                res+="\n"+exp
        elif mod=="-":
            if exp=="":
                while res.endswith("\n"):
                    res=res[:-1]
            else:
                res+=exp
        elif mod==" ":
            if exp!="":
                res+=" "+exp
        else:
            res+=exp
        i=j
    return res
